title: Wedjat eye-first deepening: deity/side polarity, hybrid anatomy, and exclusivity-model audit

research_pivot.question: Is Wedjat historically a fixed left-Horus/moon or right-Ra/sun token, or is the restored/sound eye a context-dependent motif whose side, deity and solar/lunar associations vary?
research_pivot.reason: A fixed-side assumption would contaminate morphology/orientation tests. The side/deity layer must be audited before using orientation as a historical feature.

source_ledger.note: Ptolemaic object description explicitly decomposes human and falcon elements.
Independent textual anchor for the v0.4 spiral-position chronology canary.
Ancient religious-text translation/gloss; demonstrates that Wedjat identity is not safely reduced to one modern deity/side slogan.
Composite amulet description; lower markings can even be transformed into falcon leg/wing while retaining Wedjat identity.
Late Period–Ptolemaic relief provides an explicit solar-context control.
Purposive existence audit only; not a random or exhaustive prevalence sample.

H_LEFT_HORUS_MOON_ONLY.description: Wedjat is exclusively the left eye of Horus and exclusively lunar.

H_RIGHT_RA_SUN_ONLY.description: Wedjat is exclusively the right eye of Ra and exclusively solar.

H_FIXED_SIDE_ONLY.description: Wedjat has one invariant physical side/orientation in all amuletic use.

H_RESTORED_EYE_CONTEXTUAL_IDENTITY.description: Wedjat is best treated as a sound/restored-eye motif whose deity, side and solar/lunar associations can be context-dependent rather than mutually exclusive.

H_HYBRID_ANATOMY.description: The canonical Wedjat combines a human eye core with falcon-derived markings rather than being a simple human-eye icon.

orientation_audit.note: The audit establishes existence of right, left, and double-sided forms. It must not be used to estimate population frequencies. Separate British Museum Naukratis catalogue comments state that left Wedjat eyes are usually rare in that corpus.

logical_probe_result.highest_admissible_claim: Within this source-qualified audit, mutually exclusive simplifications such as 'Wedjat = only left Horus/moon', 'Wedjat = only right Ra/sun', or one invariant physical side are incompatible with the admitted evidence. A contextual model is better supported: Wedjat is a sound/restored eye motif associated with Horus in amuletic descriptions, can be glossed as the right eye of Ra in Book of the Dead chapter 17, occurs in right, left and double-sided amulets, and participates in solar contexts such as offerings to Khepri. Its canonical morphology is explicitly human-falcon hybrid. This does not imply that all contexts are interchangeable or that deity/side associations lack historical structure.

new_eye_model.core: Treat wedjat first as the sound/restored eye motif. Encode side, deity, solar/lunar role, and object orientation as separate contextual fields rather than collapsing them into one identity label.
new_eye_model.important_consequence: The next museum-eye corpus must record LEFT/RIGHT/DOUBLE/AMBIGUOUS orientation independently of HORUS/RA/KHEPRI/THOTH textual context. Mirroring must not be normalized away before orientation analysis.

relation_to_fraction_lane.consequence: Eye polarity and hybrid anatomy can be characterized independently before any return to 1/2..1/64. This reduces circularity.

required: Freeze an orientation-labelled museum corpus across periods before geometry scoring.
Record object side as RIGHT, LEFT, DOUBLE_SIDED, or AMBIGUOUS from catalog text/visible anatomy without deity inference.
Measure spiral and vertical falcon-mark positions without mirroring objects into a common side.
Test whether morphology differs by period after controlling for orientation and material.
Only afterward compare eye-object chronology with CSM sign chronology.
forbidden: Do not infer RA solely from right-facing orientation.
Do not infer HORUS solely from left-facing orientation.
Do not mirror all eyes before testing side asymmetry.
Do not use the purposive British Museum audit counts as prevalence estimates.
